subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should browser Control UI device identity be allowed after the UI is delivered over non-localhost plain HTTP, and if yes should that be default behavior or an explicit insecure opt-in?
rationale: The remaining change decides whether persistent operator browser identity can be trusted when the page itself may have been tampered with in transit, which is a maintainer security/product boundary rather than a mechanical hash-helper fix.

options.title: Keep secure-context requirement
options.body: Continue requiring HTTPS or localhost for browser device identity and rely on trusted-proxy, Tailscale, break-glass config, docs, and warnings for self-hosted deployments.

options.title: Add explicit insecure opt-in
options.body: Allow pure-JS browser identity only behind a clearly named insecure Control UI setting with audit warnings, docs, and tests for both default-blocked and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Allow plain HTTP by default
options.body: Remove the secure-context gate and WebCrypto digest dependency by default, accepting a broader remote-plaintext trust model for Control UI operators.

recommendation.title: Keep secure-context requirement
recommendation.body: Continue requiring HTTPS or localhost for browser device identity and rely on trusted-proxy, Tailscale, break-glass config, docs, and warnings for self-hosted deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent history on the moved Control UI gateway/device identity surface and is the best available owner for the remaining security/product boundary.
